edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - PRECEDENCE: a verbatim archive answer beats every Rule 4 trimming rule and any 'more accurate' name from your own knowledge. Copy it exactly as printed, including a leading article, a type noun, or a plain country name. In flat flashcard dumps (StudyStack and similar) the answer is the capitalized words after the clue's last word, often after a comma. Strip only a contestant tag such as 'right: Name'.

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content:
- SPELLING: write names in plain ASCII letters without diacritics, as answer keys do. Passages often show the accent dropped or garbled, so use the unaccented spelling. Exception: a verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) that prints an accent is copied as printed.
- A lake, mountain, river or sea whose bare name is also an ordinary word or adjective keeps its type noun, even when the clue lists sibling names without it. Names that identify the place alone stay bare.

edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
edits.content: - A clue that is only a head of state's or ruler's title and name, with biographical passages, asks for the COUNTRY or state he or she leads. Do not answer with the title phrase or the person's own name.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - 'They/It were once called "X" (after the town or person Y)' or 'formerly known as X': the subject pronoun is the THING that carried the old name. Answer with that thing's current common name (the food, object, group or title), never the place, person or old name already in the clue. Passages that say '<X>, now known as <name>' give it. The origin place or inventor is an anchor.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content: - Quoted lyric / quotation clues (a quoted line followed by 'to this color', 'this word'): the answer is the literal continuation of the quote. Find the line repeated across the passages and copy the words that follow the quoted fragment exactly, even if they are two words. The 'drop modifiers / shortest form' rules in Rule 4 do not apply to quoted continuations.

edits.target: Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - Numeric paraphrases: when the clue gives an approximate share or size ('about 1/5 the population', 'nearly half', 'a quarter'), convert it to a percentage or range (1/5 -> about 20%) and match it against the figures in the passages. Choose the entity whose figure fits, not another large entity from the same list.
